record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.context_brief: Cusps of reflective caustics in an ellipse
record.original_question: For a point light source in general position inside an ellipse, does every generic caustic produced by repeated reflection in the ellipse have exactly four cusps?

evidence.quote: Question 1: Is it true that each (generic) caustic by reflection in an ellipse has exactly four cusps?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be an ellipse, regarded as a billiard table whose boundary reflects light rays according to the law of equal angles. Fix a point $O$ in the interior of $C$ that is in general position (in particular, $O$ is not a focus of $C$ and does not lie on the major or minor axes in any degenerate way). Consider the family of light rays emanating from $O$ in all directions. After $n$ successive reflections off $C$, this family of rays has an envelope $\Gamma_n$, called the $n$-th caustic by reflection of the source $O$ in $C$.

For generic choices of the ellipse $C$ and the source point $O$, the caustic $\Gamma_n$ is a piecewise smooth curve whose only singularities are ordinary cusps. It is known that for every $n\ge 1$, $\Gamma_n$ has at least four cusps.

Question: Is it true that for every such generic configuration $(C,O)$ and every $n\ge 1$, the caustic $\Gamma_n$ has exactly four cusps?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by Bor and Spivakovsky (arXiv:2406.11074, 2024) proves that for any ellipse the caustic by reflection has at least four cusps located at specific tangency points with confocal conics, and proves the exact "four cusps" conjecture in the special case when the ellipse is a circle. The general elliptic case remains open: the authors explicitly state they cannot show that the four identified cusps are the only ones for arbitrary ellipses.

status_evidence.title: Cusps of caustics by reflection in ellipses (Bor–Spivakovsky)
status_evidence.snippet: Theorem 1 proves that for any ellipse there exist at least four cusps... 'we do not prove that these are the only cusps' for general ellipses. Theorem 2 establishes that for a circular billiard table, caustics have exactly four ordinary cusps.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is proven only for circles; for general ellipses only the lower bound of four cusps is established.

status_evidence.title: On cusps of caustics by reflection: a billiard variation on the four vertex theorem
status_evidence.snippet: For a generic point light source, each of these caustics has at least 4 cusps, a billiard variation on Jacobi's Last Geometric Statement.
status_evidence.claim: At least four cusps is known in the generic setting.
